proposals.impact: reduce 80% intro-load drop-off by replacing generic opener with specific friction-naming copy
proposals.observation: Over the 48-hour quiz window, 5 sessions hit the intro screen. Four left without moving past intro_load. One reached email_shown and also did not complete. That is a 0% completion rate against 5 starts. The drop is happening before people have typed a single character, which points to the intro copy failing to make the quiz feel worth the next 90 seconds. Sources are roughly split between direct and Instagram, so this is not a cold-traffic problem — these are people who already know Joel well enough to click. The intro is losing people Joel has already earned.
proposals.proposal: The intro screen is almost certainly carrying generic "find your money type" framing that could belong to any quiz on the internet. Replace it with copy that names the specific discomfort a 25-35 high-earner feels at the intro moment — the quiet dread that the number in their account does not match the story they tell at dinner. Ground it in something only Joel's biography can carry. Cut any call to action that sounds like an instruction ("discover", "find out") and replace with a single honest question that makes not clicking feel stranger than clicking.

You earn well. So why does opening your banking app still feel like bracing for bad news?

This 2-minute quiz looks at the thinking patterns that sit underneath the numbers — the ones that were probably set before you had any real money at all.

MSc Behavioural Economics | Qualified Financial Planner

proposals.impact: lift Money Worship open rate from 37.5% toward the 52-66% seen in other automations
proposals.observation: The Money Worship automation has an open rate of 37.5% against 16 sends. The Money Avoidance sequence sits at 52.6% and Money Vigilance at 66.7%. All three automations are live and enabled. The gap between Money Worship's first email and the other two is almost certainly the subject line — Money Worship is the script that says more money solves the problem, which is a common and quietly embarrassing belief for high earners. The subject line probably softens that or makes it aspirational, when the truth is that the belief feels rational right up until it doesn't.
proposals.proposal: Rewrite the subject line of email-01 in the Money Worship automation. The current line is almost certainly either aspirational ("what your relationship with money says about you") or vague ("your money type results"). Replace it with a subject line that names the specific thought pattern without shaming it — the line that makes the reader feel accurately seen rather than diagnosed. The preview text should extend the moment, not repeat the subject.

proposals.impact: add a grounded, specific in-line CTA to the freshest post before it loses peak traffic
proposals.observation: The blog post "Why do I always assume the worst about my financial future?" was committed at sha 9e13204 and published 2026-06-01 — today. It will see its highest organic and direct traffic in the next 24 to 48 hours. The post title maps directly to the Money Vigilance profile, which has the strongest open rate in the email data at 66.7%, confirming this audience is already warm and engaged. There is no evidence in the data of a contextual CTA block inside the post body linking to the quiz. A reader finishing that post is in exactly the state of quiet honesty the quiz intro should meet.
proposals.proposal: Add a short, grounded mid-post or end-of-post CTA block to the freshest blog file before peak traffic passes. The block should not feel like a banner. It should read as a natural next sentence — one that acknowledges the reader has just done something honest by reading this far, and offers the quiz as a continuation of that, not a product. No imperative verbs. No "click here". One specific sentence that earns the link rather than demanding it.
